records.question: Where does the drone beyond-visual-line-of-sight rule (Part 108) stand, and what other drone rules are pending?
records.answer: Part 108 is still only a proposal: the FAA and TSA proposed it August 7, 2025, refused more comment time September 29, 2025 and reopened comments on one design question January 28, 2026; the record holds no final rule, although EO 14307 set a 240-day final-rule target ('as appropriate'). The other pending drone rule is the FAA's May 6, 2026 proposal to restrict drones near fixed-site facilities (comments extended to August 5, 2026). 3 items are notices, not rules: Electric Vertical Takeoff and Landing and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Pilot Program — Establishment and Request for Proposals; Implementing Section 927 Waiver Process for Certain Unmanned Aircraft Operations; Unleashing American Drone Dominance (FCC Notice of Inquiry). 2 are final: Integration of Powered-Lift: Pilot Certification and Operations (SFAR); Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports.

records.question: Is DTC's tokenization live, and on which blockchains?
records.answer: Partly. DTC ran its first production trades with tokenized assets on July 15, 2026, in a limited form. As of October 19, 2026, DTCC still describes the full service as an October 2026 launch and has not announced it. Blockchains named: LFDT Besu (DTCC's private network) (live, limited, since 2026-07-15), Canton Network (public) (live, limited, since 2026-07-15), Stellar (public) (announced only, expected first half of 2027), Arc (Circle) (announced only, expected 2027).

records.question: Which federal agencies does each executive order put to work?
records.answer: The 509 Trump executive orders with agency maps (January 20, 2017 to September 29, 2026) put 163 federal agencies and offices to work. The Justice Department is named in the most orders (153), then the Office of Management and Budget (147) and the Department of Homeland Security (139).

records.question: What have courts decided about who gets a Fed account?
records.answer: So far the courts side with the Fed. Two appeals courts (the Tenth Circuit for Custodia in 2025 and the Second Circuit for Banco San Juan in 2026) held that being eligible for a Fed account does not entitle a bank to one. Custodia has asked the Supreme Court to take the case, and the Fed opposed review on October 13, 2026.

records.question: Master account, limited account or payment account: what is the difference?
records.answer: A master account gives full access to the Fed's payment services and its credit. A limited-purpose account (so far only Kraken's) gives payment access without the Fed's credit, and the proposed payment account would do something similar for a new class of firms. Without any account, a firm reaches the Fed only through a bank that has one.

records.question: Who has a Federal Reserve account, and who is still waiting?
records.answer: No crypto firm is confirmed to hold a full Federal Reserve master account. Kraken has a limited-purpose account; Anchorage Digital is waiting for a decision; Custodia Bank is fighting its denial in court.

records.question: What is each Reserve Bank studying in 2026?
records.answer: Each Reserve Bank's 2026 conference records cover a different mix of topics. Across the six themes the library tracks, AI adoption and agentic controls is the widest (8 Banks: Boston, Cleveland, Richmond, Minneapolis, Dallas, San Francisco, New York, St. Louis); digital money, clearing and finality has 6; labor flows and regional distribution has 5; data governance and authority has 4; fraud, cyber and operational resilience has 4; power and physical infrastructure has 3 (Dallas, Minneapolis, San Francisco). Philadelphia falls under none of the six: its records are on mortgage transmission and intermediation. A conference topic shows what a Bank is paying attention to, not that it owns the function or has adopted a policy.

records.question: How big is FedNow now, and how fast is it growing?
records.answer: FedNow settled 4,997,811 payments worth $274.664 billion in the second quarter of 2026 (54,921 a day), up from 2.7 million payments worth $271.3 billion in the first quarter. There were more than 1,800 live institutions by mid-July 2026 (about 1,600 in January), and the largest payment allowed rose from $500,000 at the July 20, 2023 launch to $1 million in March 2025 and $10 million in November 2025. The library holds only these two quarters of volume, so it cannot show a longer growth trend yet.

records.question: Can the President fire a Fed governor?
records.answer: Only for cause, and only after notice and a chance to respond. On June 29, 2026 the Supreme Court (5-4) kept Governor Lisa Cook in office, holding that courts can review the 'cause' and that she got no notice or hearing. On October 7 the President set up a committee to try again, with a hearing set for November 5, 2026.

records.question: What did each House hearing on the Fed set out to change, and who testified?
records.answer: The library records 11 House Financial Services hearings on the Fed, from March 4, 2025 to June 25, 2026: 9 by the Task Force on Monetary Policy and 2 by the full committee or a subcommittee. The Task Force heard 45 witnesses, and the library reads 12 of them as 'Analytical'; each card gives the witness's affiliation, a quote, and links to the committee memo and transcript.

records.question: Which Fed technology projects are live, and which are only proposed?
records.answer: Of 17 Fed technology projects the library tracks, 9 are live (FedNow and its add-ons, the Reserve Banks' shared AI platform, Richmond's national IT, the New York repo platform, Philadelphia's collateral systems, Treasury central clearing and DTC's tokenized entitlements), 1 is an authorized but limited account (Kraken), 2 are scheduled (the 2027 FedNow discount and longer Fedwire hours in 2028 or 2029), 2 are proposals (the Payment Account and the Fed's stablecoin rules) and 3 are research only.
